newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA RECOVER AFTER SHAKY START.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA RECOVER AFTER SHAKY START.

text.p: South Africa recovered from a shaky start to reach 70 for one at lunch on the opening day of the first test against India on Thursday.
Put in on a hot and humid morning, South Africa were reduced to eight for one in the fourth over when Gary Kirsten was bowled by a Venkatesh Prasad inswinger for two as he pushed forward defensively.
But South Africa then rallied with opener Andrew Hudson 34) and Adam Bacher (25) putting on 62.
Earlier, the South African batsmen had been under extreme pressure on a pitch offering pace and bounce to the new ball, while the humidity allowed the ball to swing.
Hudson played and missed at the third ball of the innings bowled by Javagal Srinath and then survived a confident shout for leg before off the final ball of the same over.
But South Africa, who omitted wrist-spinner Paul Adams and batsman Jacques Kallis from their 13, recovered with confidence as the pitch began to flatten out after the opening hour.
Bacher, making his test debut at the age of 23, batted with geat composure.
Both batsmen were particularly fluent through the offside and relished batting in front of a capacity crowd of 20,000 -- a test record at Kingsmead.
Bacher, South Africa's most prolific batsman in the domestic Supersport Series this season, hooked a short ball from seamer David Johnson for six to bring up the 50 in the 21st over.
